bobkit_architect_workflow.overview: The BobKit-Architect mode orchestrates the planning, task generation, checklist creation, and analysis phases of the BobKit lifecycle. This workflow ensures specifications are translated into actionable, validated implementation plans before code is written.

mode_responsibilities.responsibility: Convert specifications into structured implementation plans
Generate dependency-ordered task lists from design artifacts
Create domain-specific quality checklists for requirements validation
Perform cross-artifact consistency and quality analysis
Validate technical soundness and architectural coherence
Manage transitions to implementation modes when ready

phase.name: plan
phase.purpose: Execute implementation planning workflow using plan template

step.action: Run setup script to get feature paths and branch info
step.validation: Verify FEATURE_SPEC, IMPL_PLAN, SPECS_DIR, BRANCH paths

step.action: Load context from spec and constitution
step.validation: Ensure all required sections are present

step.details: Mark unknowns as "NEEDS CLARIFICATION" for Phase 0 research
Resolve all NEEDS CLARIFICATION items through research
Run agent script to update AI assistant context files
Output branch, plan path, and generated artifacts

phase.name: tasks
phase.purpose: Generate actionable, dependency-ordered tasks from design artifacts

step.details: Read plan.md, spec.md, and optional artifacts

step.action: Extract tech stack and project structure from plan
Extract user stories with priorities from spec
Map entities to user stories (if data-model exists)
Map endpoints to user stories (if contracts exist)
Generate tasks organized by user story
step.details: - Phase 1: Setup tasks - Phase 2: Foundational tasks (blocking prerequisites) - Phase 3+: One phase per user story (priority order) - Final Phase: Polish and cross-cutting concerns
Identify tasks that can run concurrently

step.validation: Each user story has all needed tasks and is independently testable

step.details: Output tasks.md path, task counts, parallel opportunities, MVP scope

task_format.rule: Every task MUST follow: - [ ] [TaskID] [P?] [Story?] Description with file path
Task IDs are sequential: T001, T002, T003...
[Story] label (US1, US2, etc.) for user story phase tasks only
Description must include exact file path

phase.name: checklist
phase.purpose: Generate custom quality checklists for requirements validation
phase.concept: Checklists are "Unit Tests for Requirements" - they validate the quality, clarity, and completeness of requirements, NOT implementation correctness.

step.details: - Derive from user phrasing and extracted signals - Only ask about information that materially changes checklist content - Skip if already unambiguous in user input - May ask up to 2 more follow-ups if scenario classes unclear (max 5 total)
- Derive checklist theme (security, review, deploy, UX, etc.) - Consolidate explicit must-have items - Map focus selections to category scaffolding
- Load only necessary portions relevant to focus areas - Prefer summarizing long sections - Use progressive disclosure

- Create checklists/ directory if needed - Use short, descriptive filename (e.g., ux.md, api.md, security.md) - Number items sequentially starting from CHK001 - Each run creates NEW file (never overwrites)
Output checklist path, item count, focus areas, depth level

checklist_principles.principle: Test requirements quality, NOT implementation correctness
Ask about what's WRITTEN (or not written) in the spec
Focus on completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, coverage
Minimum 80% of items must include traceability references
Use question format asking about requirement quality

phase.name: analyze
phase.purpose: Perform cross-artifact consistency and quality analysis

step.validation: Abort if any required file missing

step.details: - From spec: Overview, Requirements, User Stories, Edge Cases - From plan: Architecture, Data Model, Phases, Constraints - From tasks: Task IDs, Descriptions, Phases, File paths - From constitution: Principles and normative statements
- Requirements inventory with stable keys - User story/action inventory - Task coverage mapping - Constitution rule set

levels.level: CRITICAL: Constitution violations, missing core artifacts, zero coverage
HIGH: Duplicates, conflicts, ambiguous security/performance, untestable criteria
MEDIUM: Terminology drift, missing non-functional coverage, underspecified edge cases

sections.section: Findings table with ID, Category, Severity, Location, Summary, Recommendation
Metrics (total requirements, tasks, coverage %, issue counts)

step.details: - If CRITICAL: Recommend resolving before implementation - If LOW/MEDIUM: User may proceed with improvement suggestions - Provide explicit command suggestions
Ask user if they want concrete remediation edits (do NOT apply automatically)

phase.constitution_authority: Constitution is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Conflicts are automatically CRITICAL and require adjustment of spec, plan, or tasks - not dilution or reinterpretation of principles.

transition.reason: Ready to convert spec into implementation plan
Generate actionable task list from design artifacts
Validate consistency and quality across artifacts

transition.trigger: All planning artifacts validated and ready
transition.reason: Begin implementation with validated plan and tasks

key_principles.principle: Create clear dependencies and execution order
Use progressive disclosure to manage token efficiency
Provide clear next actions and transition points
